entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: One composer. The role page had two more and neither was any good
entries.body:
Dan: 'we have a real consistency problem when i want to draft and send notes.
it should be universal and it should be the same container. its way too
fragmented. i have asked for rich text capabilities always.'

He is right, and CLAUDE.md already said so - 'people-work happens on the
contact page, do not grow a second correspondence UI on the role'. It had grown
two. CorrespondenceEditor was a plain textarea with its own save, refine, send
and mark-as-sent. CorrespondenceDraftForm drafted with Claude straight into it.
Neither had rich text, a signature, attachments or copies, all of which the
contact composer has had all along.

My response for most of today was to bolt escapes onto them rather than remove
them: an Open in composer link, and then a second copy of that link because the
first sat below the fold of a 60vh textarea. Two patches to avoid one deletion.

Both surfaces are now records with doors. The editor shows the note and links
to the composer; the draft form is a row of Write to X links. Deleting stays on
the role, since that is history rather than writing.

Also fixed the memory he raised twice. Instructions lived in component state,
so they survived exactly as long as the page did - reopening a saved draft
started the conversation over, and he had been reopening it all afternoon.
Correspondence.instructions stores them with the note and the composer seeds
from it. Verified end to end: two instructions written to a draft, and both
reach the client on reopen.

The declaration order bit again on the way, the same temporal dead zone as the
signature this morning. TypeScript caught this one; React would not have.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: A saved draft the page never showed you
entries.body:
Dan asked whether the notes being drafted for him were meant not to appear in
the UI. They were not meant to disappear; they were simply unreachable. A
saved draft could only be opened at /contacts/<id>?write=1&edit=<id>, a URL
nobody has unless something hands it to them, and the contact page listed
nothing. Same fault as a page nothing links to, which he caught earlier today
on /linkedin.

Saved drafts are listed on the contact page now, with their subject, an opening
line and a link that opens them in the composer.

Two things I was doing that made it worse. I deleted and recreated the draft
each time I revised it, so the id changed and any link he already had went
dead - and had he edited one, I would have destroyed the edit. And I kept
handing him URLs instead of noticing that the page had no way to surface what I
was creating.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: An outreach asks for something. I invented the rule that it should not
entries.body:
Dan hated the draft, and the fault was mine at the design level rather than in
the wording. He said Maya suggested he tell a contact he was applying. I decided
the tasteful move was courtesy with no request, wrote 'Make NO request' into
the prompt as a hard rule, and added 'do not restate how they met' - which
blocked the exact opening he wanted. He never asked for either. What he wants
is for her to push him through the process.

The drafts then did the two things he called out. 'I wanted you to hear it from
me' presumes a friendship after one conversation. And the closing offered to
send HER things, which is the ask pointing backwards.

So role_outreach now says the ask is the point, to state it once without
apologising, and that a note carefully avoiding the request wastes the
relationship and reads as coy. It opens from the conversation they actually
had, warmly and specifically. And it must calibrate to how well they know each
other, with 'I wanted you to hear it from me' named as the thing not to write.

Warmth about the conversation is encouraged; invoking a favour Dan did for them
stays banned. Those are different, and the previous prompt collapsed them.

The lesson worth keeping: I encoded my own etiquette judgement as a constraint
in a prompt, where it was invisible and applied to every future note. A
preference of mine is not a rule of his.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: A prompt nobody can select is not a feature
entries.body:
Dan asked where to send the a contact outreach and said the contact page looked
the same as before. It did. I added a role_outreach type with its own prompt,
and the only place a type can be chosen is the role page's draft form - so the
page he actually writes from was unchanged, and the draft I showed him existed
only because I called the API directly.

Worse, the contact draft route ignored type entirely. A thank-you, a check-in
and an 'I am applying' note all came out of the same prompt in the same
register.

So the composer has a type picker, and that route honours it. role_outreach is
the one with real rules and they are all prohibitions, because the failure mode
is a note that asks for something.

Two things the first real drafts exposed:

The prompt said never to mention a favour between them, while the context
handed one over: a contact's contact record says Dan gave her a reference for Maya
a former colleague, and the route feeds contact notes to the model. It duly opened with
'after we spoke when I gave a reference for Maya a former colleague' and then credited Maya
with an introduction a contact made. The prompt now says the context WILL contain
favours, that they are there so it knows who the person is, and that naming one
is the worst thing it can do - with the real failing sentence quoted, which is
the only thing that has ever worked on this model.

And the subject came back empty because unsent DRAFTS were being counted as
conversation. One saved draft was enough to convince the route a thread existed,
so it skipped drafting a subject for a first message. It also meant Claude was
reading Dan's unsent words back as though the recipient had seen them. Sent and
sent_externally only now.

Subject parsing also only existed on one of the two routes, so a note drafted
from a role arrived with 'Subject:' sitting at the top of its body.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Clear the never-consider list, and stop the LinkedIn page being unreachable
entries.body:
A Starz role came back as a pass 'regardless of fit' because Starz was on the
ruled-out list. Dan did not remember putting it there, and the list explains
why: 'Mars (Director-level step-down)', 'Ford Director AI', 'Marvin Love hotel'.
Those are roles he declined once, recorded as employers he refuses. Sixteen of
them, and only four were ever tracked in the pipeline.

The distinction he wants is real: ruled out should mean a company he would
never work for, and that is his to set rather than something accumulated from
old decisions. The list is empty, the mechanism stays, and the sixteen are kept
in personalLogistics as history explicitly marked as not a rule.

Re-evaluated Starz on the merits: swing, not pass. The honest gaps are domain
(aviation and telecom against a posting scoped to media and streaming),
campaign orchestration for entertainment releases, and 220 to 260 against a
Managing Director seat. Never a pass on the merits, and not obviously a yes -
which is the point of it being his call.

Also: /linkedin was reachable only by typing the URL. Dan asked whether it was
an orphan; it was. It sits under Profile now, not Settings, because Settings is
accounts and configuration and this is his career record.

And it takes the export files rather than a paste. The download arrives as a
zip of CSVs, and asking him to open each one and paste it is asking him to do
the computer's job. Read in the browser and concatenated with their filenames,
so there is no upload endpoint and nothing about his career sits on a disk it
did not need to touch.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: A note saying you are applying is its own kind of note
entries.body:
Dan gave the a retailer's CMO a reference for a friend, she introduced him to someone
on her team, and a a department store's posting then appeared. Telling her is
courtesy. Asking her for anything, days after she did him a favour, converts a
relationship into a transaction - and the existing types could not express the
difference, so the drafts came out as either a cover letter or a request.

role_outreach names the exact posting, makes no request, and never mentions the
favour in either direction. Four sentences at the outside, because the length
is part of the message.

The first real draft then did something worth catching: it ended with
'[Dan: add a line here with one specific detail from your conversation...]'.
Good advice, addressed to the wrong person, sitting inside an email body bound
for a CMO. general-documents already refuses bracket placeholders before filing
a document; correspondence never checked, and correspondence is the path that
reaches a stranger. stripDraftNotes removes whole lines wrapped in brackets and
leaves inline parentheticals alone, so 'the CDP (Adobe Experience Platform)
migration' survives and a note to himself does not.

Also recorded the relationships, which existed only in Dan's head: a contact
a contact as CMO of a retailer's rather than a department store's - the posting is a sibling
brand, so she is a route in and not the decision - Erin a contact as the person
she introduced, and Maya a former colleague as where the whole chain started.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: An evaluation that ran out of tokens threw away 22 seconds and said nothing
entries.body:
Dan pasted a a department store's posting and got no evaluation. The role, the job
description and the document were all created; the verdict was not.

max_tokens was 1200. That posting produced a long fitSummary and ten strengths,
the response hit the ceiling mid-object, and the tool input arrived with gaps
empty and recommendation missing entirely. Prisma refused the insert and the
route 500'd, so real model work was discarded and the UI reported nothing
useful.

strict: true and a required list do not survive truncation. The JSON simply
stops, and what arrives is a well-formed object with its most important field
absent - which is exactly why this codebase already has a rule about validating
tool output before persisting. The evaluate route was interpolating
recommendation straight into a create.

So: 3000 tokens, a usability check on the verdict before it can reach the
database, one retry at 4000 because truncation is a length accident rather than
a disagreement, and a clear 502 saying nothing was saved if it still comes back
without one. The compare path skips a truncated verdict rather than letting it
take the other model's good one down with it.

Verified by re-running the exact posting that failed: HTTP 200,
recommendation swing.

Also added the LinkedIn comparison Dan asked for. Profile pages return an
authwall and HTTP 999 to any reader, and no API exposes profile content, so it
takes a paste or the LinkedIn data export. The model only extracts; whether two
date ranges agree is checked in code, because that is checkable and a tenure is
the one claim a recruiter can verify in ten seconds. Tested against the real
variant: an exact match with different month spellings, a wrong start year, a
promotion where only the newer title is listed, and Delta still showing Present.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Draft a subject, remember the instructions, and actually write US English
entries.body:
Four things Dan hit while drafting a note to Marie.

The subject stayed blank on a new thread. It is derived from what a reply
answers, and a first message answers nothing, so nothing downstream could
produce one. The model is asked for a leading 'Subject:' line when there is no
thread, which the existing parser already strips - rather than adding a second
field to the tool, since asking one call for a subject and a body is what put
the whole body in the subject once before.

Each instruction arrived alone, so the previous one was forgotten: 'make it
shorter' then 'mention the referral' produced a short note with no referral.
The composer keeps what he has asked for while writing one message and sends
all of it, capped at six so a sitting's nudges cannot crowd out the thread that
keeps the draft factual. Recorded only on success, cleared when the composer
resets.

British spellings kept arriving despite the prompt. toUSSpelling was too short
to be the enforcement it claimed to be: whilst, amongst, towards, colour,
favour, catalogue, practise, cancelled and twenty more sailed through. The
dictionary is roughly three times the size now and covers -our, -ise, -ence,
doubled-l participles and the common adverbs.

And the rules he keeps repeating - US English, complete sentences, never
ending on a preposition - were in one route's prompt. They are in
standingPreferences now, which buildProfileContext feeds to every model call,
so the resume, the cover letter, the assistant and the Ask box all get them
rather than just this one.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Keep the signature when Claude rewrites the body
entries.body:
Dan composed a note to Marie with the box ticked and no signature in the draft.
He had to untick and retick to get it back. Third loss for this feature, second
from a different path.

draftWithClaude did a bare setHtml with the model's text, discarding the
signature block while includeSignature stayed true. The checkbox was telling
the truth about intent and lying about the document, which is the same failure
as the first two wearing different clothes.

Three times in one feature is a design signal rather than three bugs. The
signature lives inside the body, so every writer of the body owns it.
replaceBody is now the single writer that does; an append is deliberately not
one, since a forward adds to what is there.

audit.ts fails on a bare setHtml that neither takes an updater nor builds the
signature itself. Its first version reported all five call sites because it read
only to end of line and the safe ones wrap across several - tightened to a
window, then verified both ways: silent on the fixed code, and it catches the
exact bug when reintroduced.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Check the share intake's own failures, and gate shipping on the checks
entries.body:
The share-target change went to production with a lint error and an unchecked
fetch in it. Both were caught by eslint and audit.ts - which were running on the
same shell line as the push, so their output arrived after the deploy had
already happened. Running a check and passing it looked identical.

The unchecked fetch is the fault this codebase already has a rule about. A
failed document generation left the role tracked and evaluated, which is
indistinguishable from success until he opens it to apply and finds no resume.
It reports now, and so does a failed evaluation, matching what the paste box
already does. The <a> to a local route became a Link.

scripts/ship.sh runs build, lint and audit and exits before committing
anything. A check whose result you read afterwards is not a gate.

Its own first run failed, on 'grep -E "[0-9]+ error"' matching '0 errors'.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Freeze changelog

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Share a job link into the app instead of copying it
entries.body:
Dan noticed LinkedIn mobile can share a job by email or text and desktop
cannot, and that Counsel never appears in the share sheet.

/share runs the whole intake on a link from outside: track, evaluate, and draft
unless the verdict is a pass. Three doors point at it, because only one is a
standard.

share_target in the manifest covers Android and desktop Chrome. It is GET
rather than POST deliberately: a GET target is an ordinary navigation so the
session cookie travels with it, where a POST target arrives without one,
bounces to /login and loses the link.

iOS does not implement share_target at all, so the PWA can never appear in an
iPhone share sheet however the manifest is written. Worth stating plainly
rather than shipping something that quietly does not work there. A Shortcut is
the answer on the phone and a bookmarklet on desktop, and both reach the same
page.

Share sheets disagree about which field holds the link - Android often puts it
in text beside the title, url is frequently empty - so firstUrl takes the first
match across all three. Verified against every shape including a share with no
link, which lands on the paste box rather than erroring about something the
user cannot see.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Freeze changelog

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Stop remembering that the signature is off
entries.body:
Dan's note to Matt Menough at a hospitality employer went out unsigned. Second one today, and
this time caused by the fix for the first.

This morning he asked for the signature to be on by default with the state
preserved. Preserving it was the mistake. Unticking once while we were building
the feature wrote "0" to localStorage, and from then on every note opened
unsigned, silently. The saved HTML carries no signature marker at all, so it
was never a send-time loss: the composer never put one there.

Worse, it looks fine for a moment. The server renders the default, so the
signature appears, and the stored preference arrives after hydration and takes
it away. He saw it, went back to send, and it had gone.

The state worth keeping was ON. Off is a decision about one message, so it
lasts exactly as long as that message, and no stored value can quietly stop the
app signing his mail.

An unticked checkbox is also not a warning. It was sitting there, correctly
unticked, both times. "This note has no signature on it" now appears beside the
button that acts, because state belongs where the decision is.

Verified with the broken state deliberately reproduced: with "0" still in
localStorage the composer opens ticked and signed, unticking shows the warning
and removes exactly the signature, reticking restores one copy.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Freeze changelog

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Reply into the existing thread, not just Dan's copy of it
entries.body:
Dan asked whether replying in the app would land in the thread Matt already
started. It would not have.

The send route passed Gmail's threadId, which keeps the message in the right
conversation in Dan's mailbox and does nothing for the recipient. Every other
client, and every ATS, threads on In-Reply-To and References, which carry the
RFC Message-ID and were never being set. His reply would have arrived as a
brand new message with no quoted history, and for an iCIMS address nothing
tying it to the requisition it answers.

latestMessageRef reads the newest Message-ID in the thread at send time rather
than storing it, so it stays right when messages have arrived since the draft
was written, and it needs no migration for something Gmail already holds. It
returns null on any failure, because threading is a nicety and sending is not.

The a hospitality employer draft is attached to Matt's thread. A survey found no other
unsent draft with the same gap, so this is a fix for the next one rather than a
backlog.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Freeze changelog

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Correct a false tenure in CLAUDE.md, and pin the real dates
entries.body:
This file said "Nine years at Delta". Delta is Aug 2022 to Jun 2026, three
years and ten months. The nine years is Charter, Jan 2013 to May 2022.

I read that sentence back and put "Nine years at Delta" into a draft note to a
recruiter at a hospitality employer. Dan caught it. A tenure is a verifiable claim about his
career: wrong in front of an employer it is checkable on LinkedIn in ten
seconds and reads as careless or dishonest, which is worse than any formatting
fault this file catalogues.

The data was right the whole time. Both variants carry the correct dates, and
a tight sweep of 347 documents, 4 variants and the profile found no wrong Delta
duration anywhere - the letters say "four years at Delta" and "nine years at
Charter" correctly, including one that states both in the same sentence. The
error existed only in the prose describing the data, which is what gets skimmed.

So the dates are now stated once, near the top, as the thing to read rather
than recall, with the rule that a duration must be computed from them and never
remembered.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Freeze changelog

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Strip em-dashes from correspondence in code, not by asking
entries.body:
Dan has told me twice today never to use em-dashes, and I put one in a draft
note to a recruiter anyway. Worth fixing the app rather than only the habit.

All three correspondence prompts already say no em-dashes, and nothing checked.
That is precisely the pattern this codebase has a rule about: a prompt
instruction is a request, and when the model getting it wrong produces
something silently wrong rather than an error, repair it in code.

enforceHouseLanguage already does exactly this - dashes to hyphens, British
spelling to US - and was wired only to the document routes. It now runs on the
contact draft, on correspondence creation and on correspondence refine, so
anything the app writes to a person goes out in house style whether or not the
model cooperated.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Stop letting Gmail's Promotions tab decide what is a job
entries.body:
a hospitality employer's talent acquisition manager invited Dan to an initial call at 5:57pm.
The sync never saw it, and answered "nothing found" twice while he asked where
it was. He found it himself, in Promotions.

The sync query excluded -category:promotions -category:social, which was added
to cut noise and quietly handed Gmail's tab heuristic the decision "is this
about a job". Gmail is worst at precisely the mail that matters: Matt's message
came through iCIMS, and anything sent by an ATS carries tracking and
unsubscribe headers, which is what Gmail sorts on. The misfiling is systematic.

Meanwhile this app runs a classifier whose entire job is that decision, and the
Inbox already hides whatever it marks not_job_related. Filtering upstream was
doing the same work twice, worse, and invisibly.

Removing it pulled in 7 messages the sync had never been able to see. Six were
noise the classifier binned correctly - LinkedIn invitations, a cupcake sale -
and one was the interview invitation. The filter was buying six ignored rows a
day and costing that.

Also recorded what only existed in Dan's head: Matt's outreach is warm. Marie
Benton told her father, Dan's neighbour, that Matt would be in touch, so the
ATS email is the front-door version of an introduction already made. That is on
the role, on Marie's record, and Matt is a contact now.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Seed ruledOutCompanies as JSON, not prose
entries.body:
Every AI route on the demo returned 500 with "Unexpected token 'N', 'None.' is
not valid JSON". I had seeded ruledOutCompanies as the sentence "None." and
that field is JSON.parsed in two places - profile-context.ts, which builds the
context for every model call, and the Profile page.

The failure surfaced nowhere near its cause: a bad string in the seed took out
evaluation, drafting, Ask and the assistant equally, with a parser error naming
none of them. Seeded as "[]" now, and the live demo's row was repaired in
place.

Worth noting for anything else that seeds this table: several Profile columns
hold JSON in a String, and nothing in the schema says so.

Confirmed after the fix by running a real evaluation against the deployed
demo: HTTP 200, and the row records
model=claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, so the demo override is genuinely in force
rather than merely compiled in.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Freeze changelog

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Demo runs on the cheap model, with a daily cap that is the real protection
entries.body:
Dan asked whether the demo should mock the AI or use the cheapest model.
Cheapest model, because the evaluation and the drafting ARE the product.
Somebody trying the demo will paste a job link and expect a real verdict, and a
canned paragraph is either obviously fake or - worse - looks real while being
the same text for every posting. Haiku is roughly a fifth of Opus per token and
still visibly does the job.

But the model choice only changes the cost per call, and volume is the actual
exposure: the demo runs on Dan's API key, so an open link is an open invoice.
Hence a daily cap of 60 generations, counted off rows the demo actually wrote
today rather than an in-process tally, which resets on every cold start and
therefore caps nothing on serverless.

Both live in resolveModel, because every AI route already calls it before it
spends - the same reasoning that put the outbound guards inside sendMail and
driveFetch rather than in each of a dozen callers. generateStructured gets its
own, since the Gemini path does not pass through resolveModel and would
otherwise be an uncapped way to spend.

Demo mode also ignores the model picker outright. Letting a visitor select Opus
would hand them a five-times-more-expensive button on Dan's key.

Verified in both modes: the cap fires at 60 and above with DEMO_MODE=1, and
never fires without it.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Freeze changelog

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Give the demo its own way in, since Google login is locked to one address
entries.body:
Real login is Google OAuth restricted to ALLOWED_EMAIL, which is right for a
single-user app and useless for a link Dan hands to somebody: they would have
to be him. Registering a second redirect URI for a demo domain would also drag
Google Cloud into it, and the demo is meant to stand alone.

So demo mode swaps the Google button for a shared password. Not to protect the
data - it is invented and worth nothing - but to protect the spend. Every page
in here can call Claude, and an open URL is an open invoice.

`/api/auth/demo` 404s when IS_DEMO is false, so it is not a second door into
the real app. Verified rather than assumed, since that is the whole security
claim: with DEMO_MODE=1 a wrong password redirects to ?error=bad_password and
the right one issues the ordinary session cookie; without it, the same POST
returns 404 and the real landing page still offers Google and nothing else.
Signed out, the demo shows the password form and none of the pipeline.

Two bugs of mine on the way here, both fixed:

The setup script wrote the connection string unquoted. Neon URLs end in
"&channel_binding=require", and an unquoted ampersand makes the shell
background the assignment when the file is sourced - the variable silently
never gets set, with no error until something reads it.

And my first attempt at running the demo set DEMO_MODE=1 and let `next dev`
load .env.local, which points at production. That would have served Dan's real
pipeline under a banner saying it was sample data, which is precisely the
failure this mode exists to prevent. scripts/demo-dev.sh exports the demo
values explicitly and refuses if they match production; relying on file-loading
order was the wrong instinct for something this consequential.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: One command to stand the demo database up, with the URL never in chat
entries.body:
Dan picked a separate Neon database over a shared schema, which is the right
call if this is going anywhere: the demo becomes independent infrastructure
rather than a naming convention.

scripts/demo-setup.sh reads the connection string off the clipboard, so it
never passes through the conversation or a shell argument that would land in
history. It refuses anything that is not a Postgres URL, and refuses outright
if the clipboard matches the string already in .env.local - pointing the demo
seeder at production is the one mistake this whole setup exists to prevent, and
it is now caught three times over: here, by DEMO_MODE, and by the seeder's own
real-records check.

.env.demo is covered by the existing .env* ignore.

No dotenv-cli. The script reads .env.demo into the environment itself, since
Prisma takes DATABASE_URL from there and a dependency for one line is a
dependency to keep updated forever.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: A demo instance, with two independent reasons it cannot reach anything real
entries.body:
Dan wants to show this to people without exposing a live executive job search:
real recruiters, real salary conversations, a real mailbox.

The demo runs on its own database with an invented candidate at invented
employers, and `DEMO_MODE=1` refuses every outbound action regardless of what
that database holds. Either would probably be enough. Together, a mistyped
environment variable cannot email a stranger from Dan's Gmail, which is the
only failure here that would actually matter.

The guards are in sendMail, driveFetch and fetchRecentMessages rather than in
the routes above them, so a caller added later inherits them without knowing.
Drive needs exactly one because everything already goes through driveFetch -
that existing rule is what makes a single guard sufficient.

seed-demo.ts refuses twice: if DEMO_MODE is unset, and if the database holds
real records. Both were verified against the live database rather than
reasoned about - it declined both times and the 97 applications, 28 contacts
and 86 companies are untouched.

The sample search is shaped like one in flight rather than a tidy one: roles at
every stage, silence of different ages so the follow-up cadence has something
to say, one thread where the candidate owes a reply and one where the employer
does, one networking contact with no role behind them, one unfiled message. A
demo where nothing needs doing demonstrates none of the product.

Employers are fictional. Real brands read as more convincing for about five
seconds and then raise a question about endorsement.

All of this is inert without DEMO_MODE, so production is unaffected.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Audit every button, and fix the three faults it found
entries.body:
122 buttons across 85 files. None were dead, which was the good news; two
static flags were false positives (ApplicationPicker's submit is always inside
a parent form, ThemeSetting's onClick sat past a comment my parser stopped at).
Three real classes came out of it.

Two native dialogs were still live, on the two highest-stakes actions in the
app: confirming a send, and deleting a role. CLAUDE.md says these were all
removed. They were not, and the send one was the worst place for it - the
dialog covered the row holding the address and the attachment list it was
asking you to check.

Four destructive actions had no confirmation at all. Delete correspondence,
delete a contact, delete a document and all its versions, delete an uploaded
file. One click, no undo, in an app that stops to confirm sending an email. On
the role page the inconsistency sat inside a single row: Save was a proper
SubmitButton with "Saving...", and Delete beside it was a raw button with
nothing. All six now arm in place and name the thing - "Delete Michele
Stewart?" - with Escape to back out.

Seven submits had no pending state. SubmitButton gained a formAction prop,
which is the only reason they were hand-rolled to begin with. Log out keeps its
raw button; it navigates away.

And the primary fill was written ten different ways - eleven at text-xs, eight
at text-sm, four at text-[12px], seven more shapes once or twice each. Nothing
was broken by it, but there was no answer to how big a primary button is, so
every new one was measured against whatever was nearby. buttonClass() is the
answer across 28 files; zero hand-rolled accent fills remain.

Verified in the browser: the confirm arms with the recipient's name, the
confirm control is red, Escape disarms and restores the original.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Decide once what may be rewritten, and confirm the saves that work
entries.body:
Two reports, and both turned out to be the app knowing something and not
saying it.

"How do I edit a mail I already sent" had three answers depending on the page.
The contact page refused anything but a draft. The role page's textarea saved
straight through with no check whatsoever, so history was quietly editable
there. And "Mark as sent" wrote status "sent" directly, which CLAUDE.md
reserves for the send route after Gmail returns an id - so a note posted from
Proton was recorded as though the app had proof.

`canEditCorrespondence` follows the authority the statuses actually carry. A
`sent` row has a Gmail id: the stored copy IS the message, so it is locked, the
textarea is read-only and it says why. A `sent_externally` row is Dan's word
that he sent it from Proton, where he may have changed a line first - the copy
here is a transcription with no independent authority, so correcting it makes
the record more accurate rather than less. That one is editable on purpose,
which is the thing he was actually asking for. A Gmail id locks a row whatever
its status claims. "Mark as sent" now writes sent_externally and reads "I sent
this myself".

Verified against his real an airline thread: the Proton note stays editable, the
three Gmail-sent ones are read-only with the reason.

The contact save was never broken. His edit to a recruiter's title and
phone is in the database; the form simply never said so, which is
indistinguishable from a dead button. The button is the status now - "Save
changes" while the boxes differ from the server, "Saved" once they match. It
also had a real silent refusal: an empty name made the action return early, so
clearing it and pressing Save genuinely did nothing. Disabled, with the reason.

It was bare markup on the page background while Needs you and the Inbox sat on

inside a card.

Checked in both themes, since the panel colour is a token and a literal would
only have failed in dark: three panels, no nesting, #fff light and #121418 dark.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Make the Inbox row say which control is the point
entries.body:
Five controls in one line, all about the same size, and the loudest of them
created a job record. Dan called it: the button was in a weird spot, then it
was too small, then the whole row looked wack.

It is two tiers now. Filing is the only action that takes a message out of the
Inbox, so it gets its own line and the only accent button on the row - 152x36
and flush to the right edge, where it was previously a 60px afterthought. The
quiet tier underneath carries enrichment and dismissal, with "Not relevant"
furthest from the thing you came to do.

Labels name what they file to. "File it" said nothing about which of the two
things you had just chosen, so it is "File to this company" against "File to
this role" across the toggle. "Track this role" became a plain link reading
"Track it as a new role", offered only when a role was actually detected.

"Add as contact" was doing more than it said. It redirected to the new contact's
page, abandoning the Inbox with the message still unfiled - the one thing the
row exists to resolve. Adding somebody is enrichment, not navigation, so it
stays put, and a sender already in the book renders as a link to them rather
than offering to add them twice. Erin a contact and Kimberly Baker are in, so the
a retailer's row proves it.

Also on the pipeline: a second role at the same employer put its title in the
COMPANY column, so Marriott's "On-Site Digital Products" started where
"Marriott International" started instead of under the first role's title. Chase
and Coca-Cola read the same way. The company column is rendered for siblings
now, just empty - an omitted column collapses and everything after it slides
left. Verified at 1280: company at 89, both titles at 429. Siblings also
dropped their salary entirely, which hid a real $182,100-$305,000 range on the
second Marriott role.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Stop the Inbox assuming every message is a job
entries.body:
Dan flagged the placement of "Track this role" and, in passing, the thing that
actually mattered: the message in his Inbox is a networking coffee with a VP at
a retailer's, and there is no role behind it.

The button would have created one. `createApplicationFromMail` fell back to
`mail.subject.slice(0, 120)` for the job title, so clicking it would have put a
role called "Fw: Re: Finding Time" at a retailer's into the live pipeline at
LIVE_POSTING_FOUND and redirected him into it. Seven messages in the mailbox
have a detected company and no detected role, which is the exact shape company
filing exists for.

So: the action refuses without a detected role, the button is only rendered
when there is one, and FileMailControl stops defaulting its toggle to "role" on
a message that has an employer and no job - which was asking him to pick a job
that does not exist.

The layout request is the easy half. Dismiss sits left, everything
constructive right, primary last, verified at 1100px: "Not relevant" at 33 and
the filing actions at 978 and beyond.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Name who you are writing to, and put the recruiter first
entries.body:
"Write to them" on the AT&T role opened a hiring contact, who is vacating the job,
instead of a recruiter, who is the recruiter. It took `contacts[0]` under
createdAt desc, and both were created the same day, so it was not a choice at
all - the tie broke arbitrarily.

Sorting the recruiter first fixes this instance: a cadence follow-up asks where
the process stands, and that is the recruiter's to answer on every role here -
Michele at AT&T, Brian a search consultant at a search firm, Josephine at United, Marcelo at
a hotel group.

But the ordering is the smaller half. The real defect was the label. An app
deciding between a hiring manager and a recruiter will be wrong regularly, and
"them" made it wrong invisibly - the mistake only surfaced when the composer
opened on the wrong person. Every contact is named now, capped at three, each
carrying their role on hover: "Write to a recruiter or a hiring contact". A
named link that guesses wrong costs nothing, because you can see it first.

`recruiterFirst` is pure and covers the five real shapes in his pipeline plus
the no-recruiter case, where it leaves the order alone.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Put the way out of the plain editor where the eye already is
entries.body:
"When I hit expand its that large window thats it." Expand turns the draft into
a full-screen overlay with a 60vh textarea, and every control - Save edits,
Open in composer, refine - sits below it. The composer link was there; it was
741px down a 342px viewport, reachable by scrolling and invisible in practice.

It is in the expanded header now, beside Done. That bar is the only thing on
screen when the overlay opens, so the way from a plain textarea into the real
editor is the second thing you see rather than something you scroll for.

Same fault as ApplicationPicker: a control that opens in flow puts its own
affordances off-screen. The rule in CLAUDE.md covers closing; this is the same
idea one step further, that the actions have to be reachable too.

Also swept the em-dashes. Dan's standing preference is that they never appear
and sixteen had accumulated across eight files - picker separators, role
labels, meeting dates, the privacy page. The audit checks rendered markup for
them now, comments exempted, so the sweep does not have to be repeated.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Route the role page's note-writing to the composer that works
entries.body:
Dan drafted a check-in to Brian a search consultant from the an airline role and found no
signature control and no rich editor. He was in "Or write your own" on the role
page: a bare textarea with no formatting, no signature, no attachments and no
Claude. CLAUDE.md already says people-work happens on the contact page and not
to grow a second correspondence UI on the role. This is that second UI; it
predates the rule.

The note was also stranded, which is the part that had no workaround.
`addManualCorrespondence` never set `contactId`, and the contact page opens a
draft via `?edit=`, whose query requires one. A note written on the role could
not be reopened anywhere capable of finishing it. It resolves the recipient
against that role's own contacts now - by name, and scoped to the role, so one
Brian cannot resolve to another - and his existing draft was linked by hand so
it opens today.

"Or write your own" is a link rather than a form, and draft rows carry
"Open in composer". Nothing was gained by rebuilding a worse editor next to the
good one. The plain textarea on an existing draft stays: fixing a typo without
leaving the role is worth one control, it just cannot be the only way out.

Verified his actual draft: it loads into the composer with the signature
attached, exactly one copy, and the role page offers both routes.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Fix the composer crash the signature change shipped this morning
entries.body:
Dan clicked "Write to them" from an airline and got "This page couldn't load".
Every contact page with the composer on it was broken, and had been since this
morning's signature commit.

The `html` state initialiser reads `signaturePreference`, which was declared
thirty-five lines below it. A `const` is not hoisted, so the read hit the
temporal dead zone and the component threw
"Cannot access 'signaturePreference' before initialization" on every render.
It typechecks, it builds, and it fails only when the component actually runs -
which is why a passing build and a test of the pure helpers proved nothing. I
verified the signature logic and never opened the page.

The same line held a second fault: it read localStorage during render. The
server has no storage and must assume the default, so the two renders would
have disagreed even once the ordering was fixed. It is a `useSyncExternalStore`
now, with `true` as the server snapshot, and the stored preference is applied
on the pass after hydration by adjusting during render - not in an effect,
which is a lint error here for exactly this reason.

Verified in the browser rather than by reasoning about it: the page loads, the
signature is in the editor from first paint, unticking removes it, reticking
restores exactly one, and a reload with the preference off comes up unticked
with an empty editor and nothing left behind.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Label the paste box, which had a label all along
entries.body:
Dan asked whether the tracker needs a header saying what it is. It has one -
"Paste a LinkedIn job link", with two sentences explaining that the paste also
evaluates the role and drafts both documents - and `compact` suppressed the
whole block. Compact is the mode Today uses, so the only surface anyone types
into showed a bare input and a button reading "Track it".

That hid the part worth knowing. Pasting here is not the same as opening the
posting in a tab: it reads it, judges the fit, and writes the resume and cover
letter unless the verdict is a pass. Nothing on screen said so.

Compact now renders the same two sentences at a smaller size rather than a
shorter rewording, because two versions of one explanation drift apart.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Freeze changelog

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Say when to follow up, instead of waiting to be asked
entries.body:
Dan asked yesterday whether to chase a search firm about an airline and we agreed not
yet. This morning he asked whether the UI should indicate that somehow. Two
things made the answer bigger than a badge.

The conversation is not in the app - AskLog is empty, so the decision exists
only in a terminal transcript. And it had already expired: an airline crossed from
six days quiet to seven overnight, which under the app's own cadence is the
difference between waiting and checking in. A remembered answer to a question
about elapsed time is wrong by morning.

The cadence existed the whole time as prose inside the Ask prompt, reachable
only by typing a question about one role. It is a pure function now, read by
the role page, the Today queue and that prompt - which interpolates the
constants rather than restating them, so the advice and the line on the page
cannot disagree about what day 10 means.

The hard part was not the day count. The first version asserted four replies
owed and was wrong about all four: Brian did write last on the an airline thread,
to thank Dan for the resume, and a hotel group's last word was "we will be in
touch soon". A category tells you the kind of message, not whether anything in
it asked a question. Mail sorts three ways now - a message that asks something,
one that merely proves the thread is alive, and noise - which matters more than
it sounds, because 17 of the 19 roles with any mail have a robot as their most
recent sender. American Express needed two passes: careers@recruitment.
americanexpress.com defeats any no-reply test, and even once downgraded it left
the role reading "a short check-in is fine" with nobody to check in with.

Deciding to wait now writes a dated follow-up, which is what makes "he decided
there is nothing to do" different from "there is nothing to do". That only
works because Today stopped counting commitments that are days away: snoozing
used to convert an urgent row into a calm row that still counted, which is a
snooze that silences nobody.

46 pure-function cases cover the boundaries, the branch precedence, and every
sender shape in his real mailbox. Verified end to end in the browser, including
a snooze round trip, and the test row it wrote was removed afterwards.

The audit gets a fix on the way past: it read comments as code and reported the
new component for naming --flame in the comment warning against it.
