entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Fix Gemini document generation, and the strict-mode schema it exposed
entries.body:
generate-documents called getAnthropicClient() directly and handed it
whatever model id the picker sent, so choosing Gemini posted "gemini-pro-
latest" to Anthropic and came back an error the UI could only render as the
model name in red. It now goes through generateStructured(), which is the
dispatcher every other AI route already uses.

That surfaced a second fault. generateStructured sends strict:true, and
strict rejects minItems/maxItems other than 0 or 1, so the cover letter's
3-to-5 paragraph bound failed the whole request. toGeminiSchema already
stripped those keys; toStrictSchema now does too, and the count stays in
the field description where every other length rule in these schemas lives.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: The owed-contacts queue matched zero rows
entries.body:
Adding a recruiter at a hospitality employer exposed two independent faults in one where
clause, which together meant a contact owed something reached the dashboard
queue only if they happened to be one of five migrated warm threads.

applicationId: null was written when warm threads became contacts, since those
have no role. It also dropped every contact who is attached to one, which is
most of them - a recruiter owed a reply, or Marie, who runs recruiting at
a hospitality employer and offered to walk a resume in. The single thing that had to happen
was invisible on the page whose only job is saying what needs doing.

threadStatus: { not: "closed" } compiles to SQL <> 'closed', which is NULL
unsafe. Only the migrated threads ever had a threadStatus set, so the clause
meant to exclude finished threads excluded every ordinary contact instead. Both
faults live, the query returned nothing.

Fixed by spelling out null, and the same clause copied into /pipeline during the
route split is fixed too. Today went from "2 things need you" to 3, and the row
links to her contact page rather than the directory.

Marie is recorded with a hospitality employer as her employer, the introduction through her
father in the relationship field, and the resume handover as what is owed.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Answer the questions employer forms ask, and keep the answers
entries.body:
a hospitality employer's portal asked "in a brief statement, please explain why you are an
ideal fit for our company", which neither the resume nor the cover letter
answers, and which arrives when Dan is already inside the form.

An Application questions panel on the Work tab takes the question, drafts an
answer grounded in that role's job description, evaluation and the profile, and
lets him edit it before Copy. Copy is the primary control, not Save, because the
output is text going into their box. Keeping it is optional and worth doing: the
same questions recur, portals time out, and prior answers on a role feed the
next question so two boxes on one form do not repeat each other.

ApplicationAnswer rather than Document: those are the resume and cover letter,
versioned and filed to Drive as files. These are short answers whose question is
half the record.

Three prompt rules, each earned by a bad draft. Do not volunteer a gap, because
a screening box is not a cover letter and naming a weakness they did not ask
about hands them a filter. Name what the employer actually operates using words
from the job description, since a paragraph that fits any employer fails the
only test the question applies. And treat the word limit as a ceiling: asked for
150 it returned 174.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Give the Ask panel a close control that is there from the start
entries.body:
The Close button only rendered once there was an answer, so opening the panel
showed no visible exit - and because click-outside is deliberately disabled once
a conversation is on screen, the only way out was Escape, which nobody had been
told about. An X now sits in the panel header from the moment it opens.

This is the rule I wrote for ApplicationPicker two hours earlier and then did
not apply here: anything that opens needs a visible close, not just a keyboard
shortcut. Noted in CLAUDE.md as write the close before the content.

All four exits verified in a browser: the X, Escape, click-outside while empty,
and the trigger.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Ask can set the reminder its own advice implies
entries.body:
"Write to Brian" covered advice that says act now. Advice that says wait had no
action at all, so following "hold off until day 10" depended on Dan remembering
- which is precisely what the app exists to remove. Dan spotted the gap.

Every answer about a live role now offers "Remind me in N days", which writes a
real FollowUp and therefore appears on Today and /follow-ups with no new
plumbing behind it.

The date comes from the same cadence the advice used - day 10 minus days quiet,
floored at two so a reminder is never already missed - computed in the route
rather than parsed out of the model's prose. The button and the recommendation
cannot disagree because neither reads the other. On the real an airline question:
advice said hold off at 6 days quiet, button offered 4 days, 14 August.

Posting twice returns the existing id rather than creating a second row; a
double-click is not a second intention.

Test artifacts removed: the an airline reminder I created and the verification
asks. 23 open follow-ups, unchanged.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Ask stops agreeing with a wrong premise, and follows a stated cadence
entries.body:
Dan pasted back what the app actually told him: "You wrote to Brian a search consultant 6
days ago... so this has been sitting a full week without a reply." It cited the
right figure and then re-characterised it wrongly two clauses later, because he
had framed the question as "over a week". Agreeing with a wrong premise is the
worst thing this tool can do, since checking an instinct against the record is
the entire reason to ask.

Two rules: never restate a number as words that contradict it, and never adopt
his framing of elapsed time - the snapshot is the only source. Five runs, five
corrections to "six days".

The deeper problem was that the same facts produced opposite advice. temperature
is deprecated on this model so sampling cannot be turned down, and the real fix
was better anyway: state the cadence. Who holds the ball, under 7 days wait, 7
to 10 a check-in is fine, over 10 chase, answer today where he owes the reply.
That took five consecutive runs from split (2 go / 2 hold) to unanimous hold. It
is a default the answer may argue against, so it guides rather than dictates.

One correction to my own reporting: I flagged "10 days ago" as an error. It was
right - the snapshot said 9d that morning and a day had passed.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Ask keeps a thread you can continue and return to
entries.body:
I got this wrong twice. First I refused persistence by arguing against a chat
UI, which is a different thing. Then, having accepted persistence, I assumed the
need was a record to re-read. It was not. Dan wanted to continue the
conversation: "ok what should it say when I do" means nothing without the turn
before it.

AskLog rows now carry a threadId. A follow-up replays up to eight prior turns
into the messages array, capped so a long thread cannot crowd out the snapshot
that keeps answers factual. The panel shows the exchange stacked oldest first,
with a follow-up field, and lists earlier conversations by their opening
question, which is what you recognise a thread by rather than its last turn.

Verified end to end: turn one recommends waiting, turn two ("ok what should it
say when I do") answers in context with the actual note text, the Earlier list
shows the two-turn thread by its opening line, and resuming returns both turns
with their action buttons intact.

The migration backfills rather than drops: threadId is required, and each
pre-existing ask becomes a thread of one keyed on its own id. My verification
asks were then cleared so the Earlier list starts empty for Dan.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Ask: advice reaches the action, and every exchange is kept
entries.body:
Two things Dan pushed on, and he was right on both.

A person named in this app's advice is named because he should write to them, so
a matched contact is now a primary "Write to Brian" button rather than a link to
a page. It points at /contacts/<id>?write=1&prompt=<the question>, and the
contact page opens with the composer already up and the question in Claude's
instruction box - so the draft is one click from the recommendation instead of
something to retype. Matched roles stay quiet links; opening a role is
navigation, not the act.

On history I had argued no, and I was wrong in a specific way: I argued against
a chat UI and he was asking about persistence. Different things. The answers are
judgement calls that vary run to run - the same an airline question gave "worth a
nudge" once and "wait until day 10" the next - so without a record there is no
telling whether it changed its mind or he misremembered, and over a months-long
search it is a decision log. AskLog stores the question, the answer and the
subjects it matched. The write never blocks the answer.

Verified: the action button carries the question through, the contact page
arrives with editor, toolbar, signature checkbox and instruction all present,
and the same page without the flag stays closed.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Fix the stacking rule that broke the header, and make Ask answers survive use
entries.body:
The Ask panel looked transparent because it was rendering underneath the page.
body::before paints a fixed glow and `body > * { position: relative; z-index: 1 }`
existed to lift content above it - but that blanket rule also overrode the
header's own `sticky top-0 z-40`. The header computed to relative/1, so it was
never actually sticky, and main at the same z-index later in the DOM painted
over it. The glow moves to z-index -1 and the blanket rule goes. Two visible
faults from one line of CSS, and the header not being sticky had gone unnoticed.

Then the UX, which Dan was right to push on rather than accept.

The panel closed on click-outside, so asking "should I chase a search firm" and
then clicking the an airline role - the thing it had just told him to do -
destroyed the answer. The panel fought the action it advised. Click-outside now
only closes an empty panel; once there is an answer, dismissal is Escape or the
explicit control.

And the answer was inert prose. It named an airline and Brian a search consultant, both of
which are pages, and reaching them meant going to find them by hand - the same
fault as a count that links nowhere. The route now matches tracked company and
contact names against the text it produced and returns them as links, shown as
"Open: an airline · Brian a search consultant".

Verified in a browser: closes when empty, survives an outside click once
answered, and the links resolve to the right role and contact.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Stop asking to schedule a meeting that is already on the calendar, and make Ask visible
entries.body:
Two things Dan caught.

The Inbox was offering to add the AT&T 1:00 PM call to the calendar while an
interview note for the same role at the same minute already existed, so
confirming it would have booked the meeting twice. pendingTimes had rules for a
time that has passed and a proposal superseded later in the thread, but not for
one already booked: scheduledAt only records a booking made from that prompt, so
anything captured by the calendar sync or by hand left the prompt standing. It
now matches on role plus time within half an hour, since the booking usually did
not come from the message. Boundaries tested - 29 minutes suppresses, 31 does
not, and the one live proposal that disappeared was exactly the duplicate.

The Ask box shipped as a small button between the nav and the avatar and Dan
could not find it. He is the only user, so a control he cannot see does not
exist. It is a search-style field now, with the header rebalanced to make room:
utility links drop below lg, the field collapses to a button below sm. Measured
at 280px and 1280px, no overflow at either, and the full path verified in a
browser - field opens, example fires, answer renders.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Ask: one box, the whole search, and an actual opinion
entries.body:
Dan's example was "should I reach out to a search firm about an airline, its been
over a week" - a question the per-application assistant cannot answer, because
it spans a role, its silence, the person, and whether anything is already owed.

Read only, no tools. That is what lets the entire search go over in a single
pass: buildSearchSnapshot compresses sixty roles into about 2,300 tokens by
giving live roles detail and closed ones a name in a list, and computes
days-since for every row rather than making the model subtract dates. Silence
is what these questions are actually about.

The important part is that it does not hedge. Dan can read his own pipeline, so
a summary is worthless; the prompt demands the recommendation first and the
reasoning after, and lets it contradict the premise. On his real question it
opened with "Actually it's been 6 days, not over a week" and then argued a
nudge was still reasonable, which is the useful answer.

Two prompt rules from the first version's slips: address him as "you", since
the snapshot is written about him, and make any stated count match the list
beneath it.

A header box rather than a page, because the question occurs to you while
reading something else. Not a chat, deliberately: one-shot judgement calls, no
transcript.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Group forwarded mail by thread and stop repeating the chain
entries.body:
Dan forwards ecuris threads to Gmail as they go, so each forward carries the
whole prior conversation quoted beneath it. The AT&T thread arrived as five
messages of 976, 1851, 2705, 2904 and 4204 characters - the last containing all
of the others - and the role page showed the same sentences up to five times
with the newest reply buried on top of the history.

mail-thread.ts does two things, and is pure so both are tested against
fabricated bodies as well as the real ones.

newestPart keeps only the shallowest quote depth. In a Proton forward the
message being forwarded sits at one ">", the one it answers at two, so depth is
position in the chain and anything deeper is already its own row. The trailing
"On <date>, X wrote:" attribution goes too, since it labels the history rather
than belonging to the message. Across the mailbox: 157 bodies, 123 trimmed, 0
emptied, and every reduction over 20% was a Fw:.

groupByThread uses Gmail's threadId, which had already grouped them. Messages
in a multi-message thread now carry "thread 3 of 5" so you can see where you
are without reading the quoted history that was just removed.

Verified on the real thread: five badges 1 of 5 through 5 of 5, and Jennifer's
line appears once in the DOM instead of five times.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Edit a saved draft, and sign it by default
entries.body:
Dan corrected a note in his mail client and sent it from there, because a saved
draft in the app offered Send, Copy and Discard and no way to change a word.
The app's copy then stopped matching what actually went out.

Edit loads the draft back into the composer - the rich editor, Claude and the
Drive picker are already there - and saveContactNote updates that row when the
form carries a correspondenceId. Only a draft can be rewritten: anything with a
Gmail id, or marked sent or sent_externally, is a record of what went out, so
it falls through to creating a new draft rather than altering history.

The signature is on by default now rather than a button to remember, with a
checkbox to turn it off and the exact lines shown beside it. It is appended at
save rather than typed into the editor, so toggling it off cannot leave a stale
copy behind and toggling it twice cannot produce two. Opening an existing draft
for editing turns it off, since that draft already carries one.

Verified by driving the real server action: editing updates in place (1 row
before, 1 after, same id), and the same call against a sent message leaves it
untouched and creates a separate draft. The throwaway contact was deleted; 23
contacts, and Dan's Jennifer draft is untouched.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Draft here, reply in Proton, and record it honestly
entries.body:
Dan reads and writes his ecuris mail in Proton even though the domain is on
Google Workspace, so sending those replies through the Gmail API would file the
copy in a Sent folder he never opens and leave Proton with no record of what he
wrote. His call, and the right one: draft in the app, reply in Proton.

Two controls on a draft make that work. Copy puts subject and body on the
clipboard ready to paste. "I sent this myself" records it.

That second one gets its own status rather than reusing "sent".
POST /api/correspondence/send may still be the only thing that writes "sent",
because that word means Gmail returned an id. sent_externally is the weaker
claim - Dan says he sent it, gmailMessageId stays null, and the row reads "sent
from another client". The app should never overstate what it knows.

Everything that reads status was audited for which meaning it wanted: the
activity timeline and the role-page badge count both as gone out, the send
route and the discard guard accept only a real "sent".

Verified end to end on a throwaway contact, then deleted it: draft to
sent_externally, controls collapse, the row reads correctly. Dan's Jennifer
draft was not touched.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Claude's subject was going into the body, not the subject field
entries.body:
The draft Dan saved to Jennifer began:

  "Subject: Re: AT&T Opportunity: AVP, Customer Strategy & Marketing Analytics
   Hi Jennifer, ..."

so the subject field was empty and the word "Subject:" would have gone out as
the first visible line of the email. My doing: I removed the subject from the
tool schema after a two-field version kept putting the salutation there, and
never replaced it with anything.

The model is not wrong to want a subject, only about where it puts it, so the
leading line is lifted out and promoted rather than deleted. A subject stated
inside the body is unambiguous about which is which, which is exactly what the
two-field version could not manage.

Where the model writes none, a reply inherits the subject of what it answers,
with Re: added once. Fw:/Re: prefixes are stripped first - these threads arrive
as "Fw: Re: AT&T Opportunity...", and replying verbatim would tell Jennifer he
forwarded her own message to himself.

Dan's saved draft was repaired in place: subject set, body no longer starting
with the stray line.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Reply where the sender is known, and never offer to add Dan as his own contact
entries.body:
Two faults in yesterday's reply path, both from the shape of this mailbox.

Contacts were matched against the role's own contacts only. The two AT&T roles
hold one AT&T person each, so a sender filed on the sibling role read as
unknown. Matching is against every contact by address now.

Worse: a forward of Dan's own reply has no original sender to recover, so
fromEmail falls back to him, and the row offered "Add sender as contact" for
Dan on Dan's own message. Two of the four rows on Jennifer's thread said that,
which is exactly why the panel read as having no way to reply at all.

Own addresses - Profile contactEmails plus the connected mailbox - are now
excluded from both controls, and those rows read "You forwarded this" instead
of "Received", so the missing reply button is a statement rather than a gap.

Verified in a browser on both AT&T roles: Jennifer's thread shows two "Reply to
Jennifer a contact" and two self-forwards with no controls, Aaron's shows
"Reply to a hiring contact", and "Add sender as contact" appears nowhere.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Make the role picker closable, and let a received message be answered
entries.body:
Two things Dan hit in one sitting.

The role picker opens its list in normal flow rather than as an overlay, so it
pushes the page down. With sixty roles in it, scrolling into the list put the
trigger off-screen above him, and there was no Escape, no click-outside and no
cancel. It closes four ways now - Escape, click-outside, a Close control in the
list header, and the trigger - all six paths verified in a browser.

The Messages panel on a role showed a received email's subject, sender, date and
Claude's summary, and offered only "Move to this role" and "Send back to Inbox".
He could not read Jennifer's message and could not reply to it, which is the
whole reason to open one.

The body now renders behind a toggle. For the reply, rather than growing a
second composer beside the one that already works, the message links to its
sender's contact page where the thread and editor live. The sender is matched on
forwardedFromEmail first, so forwards resolve - the AT&T message is a forward
from Dan's own address and correctly reaches a hiring contact. Where no contact
matches, the row offers "Add sender as contact", which is the step that makes a
reply possible rather than a dead end wearing a different label.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Sign the cover letters. All 69 of them were going out unsigned.
entries.body:
buildLetterHead adds the salutation. Nothing ever added the close. So every
cover letter this app has produced ended on the last sentence of the body with
no "Sincerely" and no name, including ones already filed to Drive.

It was silent on both sides: the prompt tells the model "the app adds his name,
contact details, the date and the greeting, so do not write any of those", and
the model obeyed while the app forgot. Neither half was wrong on its own.

buildLetterSignOff now supplies "Sincerely, / Daniel Curis" using the formal
name that matches the letterhead, and the assembly strips any close the model
wrote anyway so a letter can never carry two. All 69 existing letters were
repaired by appending a corrected version, which inherits the Drive file ids,
so the files in Drive are current and the old rows stay as history.

Two audit checks so neither can recur quietly: a cover letter with no sign-off,
and an Earlier Experience entry whose shape differs from its neighbours (the
LEGO line). Every other check in there is about code; these are the first two
about what actually reaches an employer.

The preview overlay now shows a spinner while the file renders and always
offers "open in a new tab". Both preview controls work - I could not reproduce
a dead button and verified a full round trip - but Safari regularly refuses to
paint a PDF in an iframe, and a blank overlay is indistinguishable from a
button that did nothing.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Make the LEGO line match the rest of Earlier Experience
entries.body:
Earlier Experience is four lines of title, employer and dates, copied verbatim
out of the chosen variant. When I added LEGO to the variants I wrote it with a
trailing description clause and a full stop, so three entries read one way and
the fourth read another on every resume generated since.

The detail itself is fine - "15-person US/Denmark LEGO team" is on the verified
metrics list, so it was not invented. It just does not belong dangling off a
list whose whole job is to be brief.

Fixed in all four variants and masterResume. The one already-generated resume
carrying it (a hospitality employer) got a corrected version appended rather than
regenerated: append-only means the tailored bullets survive and the new row
inherits the Drive file ids, so the link is current and the old version stays
as history.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Pipeline footers match the sections above them, and three missed headings
entries.body:
Dan spotted that "Show archive" and "Recently deleted" still read as the old
style. They did: one was a bare link I had just added, the other was still a
hand-rolled <details> with an SVG chevron and its own bordered panel. Both are
now the same object as the sticky status headers above them - full-width row,
label left, count right - and Recently deleted moved behind ?deleted=1 like
everything else, so its rows are not built until asked for. No chevron SVGs
remain on the page.

Also: deleted the dead CollapsibleCard component, and gave contacts/[id],
retrospective and profile the heading scale the rest of the app now uses.
Privacy, Terms and Releases keep theirs - a 46px statement on a boilerplate
legal page would be absurd.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Drop the native dialogs, lighten Inbox and Pipeline, restyle their headers
entries.body:
Three things, all of them finishing patterns started earlier.

No more window.confirm or window.prompt. They render outside the page, cannot
be themed, and on iOS take the whole screen - and they were on the three paths
that matter most: sending a draft to a real person, discarding one, adding a
link. The confirmations are a second state on the row now, so the address you
are sending to stays visible while you decide. The link prompt is a field in
the toolbar, which also fixed a latent bug: window.prompt drops the selection
on some browsers, so the range is captured before the field opens and restored
before createLink runs.

Two more instances of hidden-is-not-unrendered, both now behind the URL:

  /pipeline   327 KB -> 167 KB   archive behind ?archive=1
  /inbox      335 KB ->  71 KB   filed and noise behind ?show=

The inbox was the heaviest page in the app, rendering its entire filing history
and noise bin on a day when there was nothing to file. Its queries are gated
too, not just the markup, with separate counts so the links still say how much
is behind them.

Contacts and Inbox get the headline treatment the other pages already had:
"23 people." and "Nothing to file." rather than a one-word title with the count
as a caption beside it.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Detail page: build only the tab you are looking at
entries.body:
The last instance of hidden-is-not-unrendered. CollapsibleSections received all
twelve panels as children and rendered three; the other nine were still
server-rendered and serialized, so standing on Work shipped Follow-ups,
Meetings and the entire activity timeline.

The tab now lives in the URL. The page reads ?tab=, panelInTab gates each
Panel, and the strip is links rather than buttons.

  Work     242 KB -> 187 KB
  Talk               164 KB
  History            108 KB

and none of them carries the others: Follow-ups, Meetings, Activity and
Messages are all absent from the Work payload now, verified.

Panel renders itself instead of being an inert marker whose props the parent
read - that indirection was what forced all twelve to exist. Counts are passed
from the page, since the other tabs' panels are no longer there to sum, and a
tab you are not standing on still has to show what is behind it.

The remembered tab is gone on purpose. It already caused the bug where a role
left on Talk reopened on Talk and History read as empty; the URL gives back the
back button and a shareable link to a role's Talk tab.

Also: the audit reported all twelve panels as orphans because it read the tab
mapping from the component it had just moved out of. Repointed, and the dead
ApplicationTabs component and usePersistedTab hook are deleted.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Give every count on Today a destination, and make the counts true
entries.body:
Dan pulled on two threads and both came apart.

"23 follow-ups with no date" linked to the first one's application, so a count
of twenty-three took you to one arbitrary role and hid the other twenty-two.
/follow-ups now holds the whole backlog, grouped overdue / scheduled / no date,
each row closable in place. A list of what you owe that cannot be cleared is a
list you stop opening.

"19 ready to evaluate" linked to "/", the page you were already standing on.
Chasing that found the worse bug: thirteen of the nineteen were
CLOSED_REJECTED and the other six were already APPLIED. /pipeline already had a
needs-verdict filter meaning a decision is still pending, and by that
definition the count was zero. The row was pure noise on the page whose only
job is saying what is worth doing. Today now shares PRE_DECISION with the
pipeline filter so the two cannot drift, and the row correctly disappears.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Put both intake paths together on Today
entries.body:
Dan spotted this: the route split left the paste-a-LinkedIn-link box on Today
and stranded "search the boards by company" on /pipeline, which is the one page
you are never adding anything from. They are the same job - track this role -
differing only in whether you happen to have a link.

The no-link path is now a disclosure directly under the paste box, which is
also the honest hierarchy: pasting is what happens almost every time, searching
is the fallback.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Detail page: sections separated by space, not eleven boxes
entries.body:
Every panel was a bordered, shadowed card, so a tab read as a stack of
containers and the eye had to find the content inside each one. The heading
already says where a section starts and whitespace already says where it ends,
so the box was doing no work. Headings become quiet uppercase labels and the
content carries the weight.

One change in CollapsibleSections covers all eleven panels across all three
tabs.

Also documents the class of fault this rework keeps finding: hidden is not
unrendered. The detail page still serializes all three tabs' panels and ships
Follow-ups, Meetings and Activity while you are on Work. Fixing that means
driving the tab from searchParams, which is a page restructure, not a component
change - noted in CLAUDE.md as the next thing.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Pipeline: one responsive row, sticky headers instead of six accordions
entries.body:
Two renderers drew every role - a <table> for desktop and a md:hidden list for
mobile - so the page shipped all 96 rows twice at 555 KB. A table was also the
wrong primitive: fixed columns fought each other, and the role title was once
starved to 76px by a salary string that would not wrap. It is one flex row now
that reflows at any width.

The six status accordions are gone. They were hand-rolled <details> with SVG
chevrons from an older idiom, they carried six pieces of open/closed state on a
page that is pure reference, and collapsing hid nothing expensive since the
rows rendered either way. Sticky section headers replace them, the iOS Contacts
pattern: one continuous list, the current status always visible, scrolling as
the navigation.

  555 KB -> 333 KB, 0 tables, 0 duplicate lists

The three remaining <details> are the hint panel, the archive and recently
deleted. Secondary content is what disclosure is for.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Theme 449 hardcoded colours, and show the conversations the headline counts
entries.body:
Two faults, one found by Dan.

The headline said "4 live conversations" and the page never said which four.
interviewStage was computed, counted, folded into the queue, and never
rendered. A count with nothing to click is worse than no count. The four now
sit directly under the statement that counts them, as plain type between two
rules, with the next meeting time where there is one.

The second is not a matter of taste. 449 uses of bg-neutral-*, text-neutral-*,
border-neutral-* and bg-white across 25 files sat alongside the token system
that already existed. :root[data-theme="dark"] moves tokens and cannot touch a
literal, so a quarter of the app rendered a light interface inside a dark one -
pale borders, near-black text, timeline dots that vanished. Same family as
bg-[var(--accent)] resolving to nothing: it type-checks, it builds, and it is
only visible in the theme nobody tested.

All of them now resolve through --tx, --surface and --line. The red error
states stay literal; they are semantic.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: IA: split the landing route into Today and Pipeline
entries.body:
The dashboard could never be decluttered because it was four products on one
route: triage, intake, the mail panel, and a sixty-role table. The nav called
it "Pipeline", naming the page after a quarter of its contents. Every previous
pass rearranged it, because nothing could be removed without making it
unreachable.

The number that settled it: / shipped 96 table rows and 12 duplicate mobile
lists to display 3 open items. 588 KB, 380 KB of it serialized payload. The
table was inside a collapsed <details>, and collapsed is not unrendered - every
row was built, sent, then hidden with CSS.

Now: Today (/) is what needs you, Pipeline (/pipeline) is every role you track,
and the 120 lines of table assembly no longer run on the landing page at all.

  /           588 KB -> 71 KB,  96 rows -> 0
  /pipeline   the table, on the page named after it

Nav is four destinations that each answer one question. Retrospective and
Profile move beside sign-out; they are occasional, and were costing two of five
primary slots.

The Today headline is one statement set large with nothing beside it. It used
to share a row with an Inbox button, which made the first thing on the page a
layout rather than a sentence.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Contacts: call the no-employer group "Other", and sort it last
entries.body:
"No employer recorded" described the database rather than the person. It also
sorted alphabetically, landing between Optimum and a hotel group as though it
were a company. It is a bucket, so it goes to the bottom.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Freeze the changelog

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Sub-group contacts by role, but only where a company has more than one
entries.body:
I argued against the role tier from a snapshot: only AT&T had contacts across
two roles, so it would have made twenty headings over one person each. Dan
pointed out that is a fact about today, not about the list. The pipeline gains
roles constantly.

So the tier is conditional rather than absent. A company with one role stays
flat; the moment a second role appears at any employer, the headings show up on
their own. People at a company who are not tied to a specific role sit under
"No specific role" rather than in a separate group, and the "on <Company> -
<Role>" label is suppressed under a role heading that already says it.

groupContacts moved to src/lib/contact-grouping.ts and is pure, so the rule is
tested with fabricated rows instead of fake applications in a live pipeline.
Writing that test found two bugs in surnameFirst, which had shipped claiming to
handle particles: "Jan van der Berg" became "Berg, Jan van der" because only
the first word of a multi-word particle was listed, and a name already in
"SURNAME, FIRST" form - how corporate directories emit them, and how Jennifer's
name actually arrived - was inverted a second time.

entries.author: Dan Curis
entries.subject: Separate where a contact works from which role they matter to
entries.body:
Maya a former colleague appeared twice and both said Disney. Two distinct faults.

The duplicate was mine: folding WarmThread into Contact copied the five
threads across without checking whether the person was already a contact, and
two were. a contact had the same problem. The copies carried the better notes
and the thread status, the originals carried the role and the application link,
so merge-contacts.ts combines them rather than picking a winner.

The Disney part is a modelling gap. The list derived an employer from the
application, so a contact attached to a role was described as working there.
Maya is a Delta colleague who introduced Dan to a VP at Disney, which is the
most valuable kind of contact in a search and the one the model could not
express. Contact.company now holds the employer and applicationId holds the
role they are relevant to.

The backfill defaults to the role's company and refuses to write when the email
domain disagrees. That caught Brian a search consultant, listed against an airline and actually
a a search firm search consultant recruiting for it. Nobody had spotted him by eye.

Grouping is by employer, with "on <Company> - <Role>" shown only where the two
differ. Company is editable on the detail page, so the next one of these needs
no script.
